newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WEST INDIES SINK TO DEMORALISING DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WEST INDIES SINK TO DEMORALISING DEFEAT.

text.p: West Indies suffered a further blow to morale on Tuesday when they were beaten by 58 runs in a limited overs match against an Australian Prime Minister's XI.

The tourists, two-nil down in the test series against Australia and without a win in the World Series limited overs competition, were comprehensively outplayed by a scratch team of Sheffield Shield players.
"It was a good game of cricket but we didn't play well. Our batting didn't have any conviction or confidence," said West Indies captain Courtney Walsh.
The veteran fast bowler said his side conceded about 30 runs to their opponents because of poor fielding.
"The way we are playing at the moment we can't afford to give anything away," said Walsh, whose side lost their first two World Series matches against Australia last weekend.
Chasing the home side's total of 258 for eight in their 50 overs, West Indies scored 200 for nine in 43.4 overs at Manuka Oval.
Fast bowler Patterson Thompson was unable to bat because of a knee injury to add to West Indies' troubles.
Brian Lara failed to lift the tourists, falling for 32 to prolong a run of disappointing scores.
All-rounder Ian Harvey was named man of the match after scoring 55 not out and removing West Indies opener Sherwin Campbell for 32.
The Prime Minister's XI, featuring players on the fringe of test or one-day selection for Australia, play a one-off fixture in the national capital each season against the touring team of the day.
Openers Matthew Hayden and Dene Hills put together a century first-wicket partnership after retired former Australia captain Allan Border won the toss.
